The race for U.S. Senate came to Laredo in its closing days, with both major candidates holding rallies in the city over the weekend to urge voters to cast ballots before early voting ends, according to KGNS.

Republican Ken Paxton spoke Friday at a Laredo restaurant to fewer than 100 people, while Democrat James Talarico spoke Sunday to a packed house at Laredo Food Park. Both candidates have been traveling across Texas in their final push before Election Day on November 3.

Paxton won the Republican nomination after defeating John Cornyn in May, ending Cornyn's 23 years in the Senate, and has served as Texas attorney general since 2015. According to KGNS, Paxton told his Laredo crowd about his "Protecting the Texas Promise Plan," which he said includes cuts to medical costs, an expanded child tax credit, and help with down payments.

Talarico has served as a Texas state representative since 2018 and is a former middle school English teacher who has described his campaign as a grassroots effort. According to KGNS, he told his crowd he would take South Texas values, including family and freedom, with him to Washington, and that his first bill would target corruption by overturning Citizens United, removing corporate PAC money, ending gerrymandering, and passing term limits.

Supporters at the rallies spoke about why they showed up. Leo Garza drove in from Oilton to hear Paxton, while Victor Martel attended the Talarico event with the national nonprofit Men 4 Choice in support of reproductive freedom. Both men told KGNS they want a representative who listens across party lines.

The Laredo rallies have ended, and the tours move on to El Paso, with Talarico there Monday and Paxton arriving November 1, according to KGNS. Early voting runs through October 30, and Election Day is November 3.

Sources:

  • KGNS, "Senate candidates make final push in Laredo before election day," October 26, 2026
